prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1329; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Officers responded to a report of a head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. Driver 1 and Driver 2 were both still at the scene when officers arrived, and Driver 1 stated that the vehicle had been struck at low speed. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated by responding medical personnel. Passenger was also present in Driver 1's vehicle, and both officers and a bystander confirmed that Passenger had been seated inside at the time of the incident.

Officers observed only minor contact between the two vehicles. Damage to Driver 1's vehicle appears on a different side and at a different height than the front-end contact described by the parties. No independent witnesses to the collision were identified, and no photographs or other reports of the event were located. Driver 1 has no known prior damage to the vehicle on record. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the applicable policy.

Officers documented the scene and released both drivers after statements were taken.
